name: Benjamin Hardin
bio: a Representative from Kentucky; born at the Georges Creek settlement on the Monongahela River, Westmoreland County, Pa., February 29, 1784; moved with his parents to Washington County, Ky., in 1788; attended the schools of Nelson and Washington Counties, Ky.; studied law; admitted to the bar in 1806 and commenced practice in Elizabethtown and Bardstown, Nelson County, Ky.; settled in Bardstown in 1808; member of the Kentucky state house of representatives in 1810, 1811, 1824, and 1825; served in the Kentucky state senate, 1828-1832; elected as a Democratic Republican to the Fourteenth Congress (March 4, 1815-March 3, 1817); elected as a Democratic Republican to the Sixteenth and to the succeeding Congress (March 4, 1819-March 3, 1823); elected as an Anti-Jacksonian candidate to the Twenty-third and to the succeeding Congress (March 4, 1833-March 3, 1837); secretary of state of Kentucky 1844-1847; member of the State constitutional convention in 1849; died in Bardstown, Ky., September 24, 1852; interment in the family burying ground near Springfield, Ky.
